chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Al Maghra, from Ibrahim Bin Maymoun, who asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him):

He said: 'The shepherd is given the sheep in the mountain to pasture them, and for him is their wool and their milk, and he gives us dirhams for every sheep.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.' So I said: 'The people of the Masjid say it is not allowed because among them are those who have neither wool nor milk.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'And is it not that he purifies it by that? Some of it goes and some of it remains.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِذَلِكَ بَأْسٌ: There is no problem with that

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a shepherd to receive a fixed salary while keeping the wool and milk of the sheep?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the practice of paying a shepherd a fixed wage per head while granting him rights to the wool and milk, addressing the concern that some sheep may not produce both. He clarifies that the compensation is justified by the overall benefit to the flock, as the shepherd’s care ensures that the aggregate yield of wool and milk offsets the periods when individual animals do not produce. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of accepting mixed benefits in employment contracts where the laborer assumes the risk of variable natural yields.
